text:
Dylan Strome doesn't win races: our tracking has his top speed in the 6th percentile among skaters. He doesn't need to. He has 14 points in 15 games for Washington, 11 of them assists, and his chance creation has jumped to 1.19 expected goals per 60, up from 0.78 last season.

That's why the goal total looks wrong. Three goals on 5.1 expected is the kind of shortfall that usually corrects, since goals tend to follow chances, and his 9.4% shooting sits below his range. His ice time over the last ten games, 18.1 minutes, is up on his season average too.

The trade-off is the familiar one. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile for primary shot assists last season, but Evolving-Hockey had opponents getting 0.19 more expected goals per 60 with him on the ice, bottom 4% of forwards. This season Washington's 5v5 share with him is 52%, a bit below its share without him. Our projection: 66 points and 20 goals.
headline: Strome is getting the looks, not the goals
